meta.title: The Supreme Court Broke Up One Oil Company. It Became Dozens.
meta.hook: In nineteen eleven, the Supreme Court ordered Standard Oil broken apart under the Sherman Antitrust Act.
meta.description: In 1911 the US Supreme Court ruled Standard Oil was an illegal monopoly and ordered it dissolved into roughly 34 separate companies. Those pieces evolved over the following century into firms including ExxonMobil, Chevron, and Marathon, among others. It remains one of the most consequential antitrust breakups in American business history.
